posts.author: TroyZ
posts.body:
it's been a while since my last visit, or should i say, my last touch to rpg maker engine. last time i do projects is in 2019. after that, real life errands come and forth that i should prioritize first. and then i abandon rpg maker entirely.
it was just last february 2026 that i being told that rpg makers hit steam at very high discounts. without thinking twice, i bought all the engines from xp to mz at one swop. naah it feels better, i got the real license now to do another projects.
it also can't be denied that we entered the era of AI bubble, really bubble, everyone everwhere is doing with AI, almost.
and then i read the very long discussion in pinned thread about AI discussion thread that went haywire
i'm now a web dev starting from 2020 (it was before AI comes out), and i do everything in my entire coding humanly, old fashioned way
seeing AI LLM that are also generative, i tried to make somethings that usually i do it manually. and surprisingly, AI do it correctly (yeah not correctly actually, you need the exact prompt and really strict pattern to guide AI from hallucinating)
now the real parts comes to me. in my journey of doing projects in this time, my strengths are in scripting (i learn it from my late teacher Theo Allen who passed away 2024 because of dengue fever), mapping, and storytelling. the rest parts, like composing, drawing, are my weaknesses.
and then comes AI generative that can do  the arts almost like nothing. yeah i know i know, every AI generative results (especially in arts) can't be tolerated because of the ethics itself. but, what about AI in scripting? how can you differentiate scripts/plugins that is human typed or AI generated, or maybe AI generated and human edited? because  nowadays, i myself use AI also, BUT not for generated ones. i just use AI in scripting just for teaching me what i should do with this parts, those parts, and the rest is my brain and my hands do the job. even debugging i do it myself until i got blocked. so, i use AI in scripting specifically for assisting me, NOT for generating what i want for me (i once do the generating parts, and it keeps changing the logic and the variables, don't want to do it again). i never touch vibe coding, and will never be. for the parts that is my weaknesses like arts, i use placeholder and built in generator until i learn how to draw myself later.
tldr; as i am the one man army that is responsible for my projects, i also use AI as assistant rather than the worker that do the generating parts. my question is, if i finish my projects (free or commercially), does my method of using AI as assistant also not ethics?

posts.author: JamesRyan
posts.body:
Not all of us can be a jack of all trades, and everyone has their own strong points, so having AI to assist in what we lack is a great idea. I almost dropped my project back in 2023 because of struggling to put my ideas into my game. And then later, with the help of AI, I could finally put them into my game and bring back the motivation to continue.
Of course, I do hate heavily AI-generated content (games, films, music, arts, etc) without any human designs or control (like some cheap games fully made by AI, with no real human efforts). People often tend to blindly hate products associated with AI, but if AI is used properly and not abused, it can be an incredibly powerful tool for independent developers like us.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
I don't have that strong a reaction about AI, but I find it funny that people are constantly trying to come up with rules to hide its usage. Like rpg maker reddit now has a rule that if you publish paid content there you have to tell if you used AI, but if the content is free you can choose to tell or not. LOL why? And STEAM changed the rules that you only need to tell for visible stuff. And many people coming up with "excuses" that what kind of use is perfectly ok even if they think art is not, and shouldn't even be mentioned. If you publish a game and used AI, give a notification how you used it and then deal with the "hate".
I also don't get the idea that you absolutely should be allowed to use AI for everything because you have no skills and it makes you sad. I mean I'd like to play chess better but I don't use Stockfish when playing because of that. I don't build a football robot with a cardboard mask of myself and send if to play in Manchester United or whatever.
But anyway, >95% users are using AI so don't worry about ethics too much. And in the future (no even right now) you'll be at a serious disadvantage if you don't use it.
PS. Here's a rank you can attach your game:
S Never used any kind of help
A Never used AI
B Used AI only to learn
C Used AI to assist
D Prompted some stuff with AI
E Prompted a lot of stuff with AI
F Prompted a lot of stuff with AI and your game still looks and plays like s***

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
Professional programmer here.
At my workplace, we are now being advised and encouraged to use AI to work more efficiently. That goes even that far that a colleague of mine recently complained he feels pressured to regularly say "Yes, I did use AI, I did not waste 5 hours/5 days to complete this work, but it only took like a couple of prompts."
Important, the rules are:
Only use AI for work that you could have done without, just by your knowledge, googling, and using StackOverflow
Let AI review your code and then decide for every potential hit whether the AI was right or not
Personally, I'm okay even with selling AI-assisted plugins as long as you understand what the AI did. The problems come when you sell stuff where you have no clue about it - I have a few people on my list.

Click to expand...
I must be one of the four people since you've helped me with code a few times here already lol. But frankly, I'd rather not use a bot to fix things: I want to gradually understand things myself (even partly).
The most I have done, AI-wise, is use someone else's work that is originally AI, and painted over it. For my mod for Classic Doom, I used it to create two backgrounds that would be a chore to create myself, and again, I had to edit and paint over stuff.
I can
understand
people using AI, because it takes many years to become decent at the many skills you need to create things like games (that is, making them solo, obviously if you're a specialist and can slot in a team, that's different). But I couldn't have started this project when I was much younger and got very far.
And though it might be a hot take: people getting incensed over AI learning by absorbing online work I always find a bit silly, because
people themselves
have done that forever and a day. There's a reason the phrase "imitation is the sincerest form of flattery" exists.
The process is just made "easier" for the completely skill-lacking end user, a bit like 3d-printing, translation software, GPS device. And much like those things, it provides an imperfect stopgap between A and B. A professional translator, manufacturer, or guide is always going to be better, much like a professional artist. But for those that value the expident (for money), of course AI is going to be a go-to solution.
